The reminder no longer fires on `git commit -m"add export handler"`. The fix is committed as `a0dd16a` on `main`.

**Cause:** `stages_all` in `src/staging.py` checked every dash-word for the `-a` letter. `shlex` turns `-m"add export handler"` into the single word `-madd export handler`, and the `a` in "add" was read as `-a`. The existing tests never put an `a` inside a message attached to `-m`, so they missed it.

**Fix:** The check now scans short-option clusters left to right and stops at value-taking options (`m`, `F`, `C`, `c`, `t` for commit). A standalone `-m` or `--message` also skips the next word as its value. Real stage-all forms still trigger: `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit -a`, `git commit -am "x"`, and `-a` after a message.

**Tests:** I added cases to `tests/test_staging.py` for messages containing flag letters, `-m -a`, and `--message -a`, plus a check that `-a` after a message still counts. The new cases failed before the fix and all 7 tests pass after it.

The commit touches only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py`, with the Haiku co-author line you specified. I left your uncommitted `README.md` note and `notes/` alone.
